dialogue.content: someone asked how I was and I answered honestly by accident.
had one call this week and it was fine.
declined a thing politely and then felt weird about it for an hour.
wrote half a message and left it in the box.
I assumed stacking long video calls would leave me socially wrung out. what actually happens is I arrive talked-out — nothing left of my own to say, so I just listen.
looked up how far away a place is instead of asking.
borrowed a charger and forgot to give it back. again.
watched something everyone had already discussed.
cleared a weekend and did very little with it.
did the laundry and answered nothing for three hours.
someone rescheduled and I was more relieved than I should admit.
stood outside a place for ten minutes before going in.
made a list of people to check on. didn't check on them.
got the train instead of driving and read most of the way.
the gatherings where people told me anything real were the ones where I said almost nothing. the ones I turned up fresh and full of my own news, I talked over everyone and came away knowing nothing.
for finding anything out, much worse.
turned off read receipts and told nobody.
swapped a call for a message and everyone was fine with it.
bought a card and didn't write in it yet.
sat in the same seat as last time out of habit.
